headline: BULLISH
headline_tag: Price above a still-falling 200-day average; leverage rebuilding

action.title: SCALE UP acquisition budget
action.detail: The market is in an early-stage uptrend with medium confidence (67/100). That supports a measured increase in acquisition spend, weighted toward active-trader and non-stablecoin channels, while keeping some budget in reserve: fewer than half of recent days closed above the long-term average, that average is still declining, short-term mood has turned warm quickly, and long-term interest rates are high. This is a budget-posture view built on past data, not trading advice and not a forecast.

reasons: BTC is 17% above its 200-day average (Mayer Multiple 1.17).
90-day return +34%; weekly RSI 60; 50-day average 9% above the 200-day.
Funding back positive (z +0.79) with Fear & Greed at 74.
Breadth only 49%; 200-day average still falling (-5% over 90 days).
watch: The tension today is between a rapidly warming short-term picture and a long-term trend that is still only partly confirmed. Sentiment jumped to +0.445, a hair under the strongly-bullish threshold, as funding swung from -0.15 to +0.79 in a single day with Fear & Greed at 74, yet fewer than half of the last 90 days (49%) closed above the 200-day average and that average is still sloping down 5% over 90 days. Glassnode-cited analysis (The Block, 29 September) placed the largest long-term-holder supply cluster at $84,000–85,000, right around today's ~$83,500 price. Breadth moving clearly above 50% and the 200-day slope turning up would confirm the read; funding running further into stretched territory without that confirmation, or price falling back below the 200-day average, would weaken it.
analysis: Short-term sentiment is bullish-leaning (+0.445 of a possible ±1), sitting just under the +0.45 line where it would be classed as strongly bullish, and it has roughly doubled from yesterday's +0.21. The main driver of that jump is funding: the z-score swung from -0.15 to +0.79 in a day, so leveraged longs are again paying a modestly above-normal premium, which reinforces the Fear & Greed reading of 74 (Greed) rather than contradicting it as it did yesterday. Positioning data reinforces the lean without looking crowded: the long/short ratio is 1.35 and open interest is about $7.98B, and The Block reported on 29 September that coin-denominated open interest was at its lowest since March, with Bitfinex analysts describing perpetual positioning as near neutral after the breakout leverage cleared, so today's funding uptick is a rebuild from a low base rather than an extreme. Liquidations stayed modest and two-sided, with TechFlow, citing CoinGlass, reporting about $281M over the 24 hours to 30 September ($145M longs, $136M shorts). Volatility is neutral for the lean: realised volatility is at the 49th percentile, Bollinger width is 18%, DVOL is 35.2 and the VIX is 16.3, while a stablecoin supply ratio of 5.4 indicates a moderate pool of sidelined stablecoin liquidity. As immediate context, The Block reported on 30 September that August core PCE rose 0.2% month-on-month (3.0% year-on-year), below expectations, with bitcoin steady around $83,700. The lean would tip into strongly bullish if funding held positive alongside the greed reading, and would cool toward neutral if funding slipped back below zero.

Medium-term momentum is bullish-leaning (+0.39 of a possible ±1), essentially unchanged from yesterday. Reinforcing that, the 90-day rate of change is +34%, weekly RSI is 59.8 (firm but well short of overbought), and the 50-day average is 8.9% above the 200-day, keeping the moving-average structure on the golden-cross side; CoinDesk noted on 30 September that bitcoin was on course for roughly a 42% third-quarter gain, its strongest quarter since late 2024. The main thing pulling against the lean is still participation: 48.9% of the last 90 days closed above the 200-day average, so the headline gain rests on a relatively recent move rather than a long run of consistent strength, though breadth edged up from 47.8% yesterday. Network and market-share data are mildly supportive, with active addresses 5% above their yearly average and BTC dominance at 58.3%, indicating activity concentrated in bitcoin rather than rotating into altcoins. Flows reinforce the lean but with fading intensity: BeInCrypto (via Yahoo Finance, 29 September) reported spot ETF inflows of about $2.98B over seven sessions from 17 September, but daily figures fell from $998.95M on 21 September to $134.47M on 25 September, and the pipeline's latest daily reading is about +$66M. The next FOMC meeting is 27–28 October, and CoinDesk reported on 30 September that the softer PCE print pulled implied odds of an October rate rise down to roughly 37–47% depending on the measure, from about 70% two days earlier. The lean would strengthen if breadth moved clearly above 50% with ETF inflows holding, and weaken if weekly RSI rolled over or daily flows turned negative.

The long-term trend is bullish-leaning (+0.24 of a possible ±1), an early and not yet fully confirmed lean. Supporting it, price is 17% above its 200-day average (Mayer Multiple 1.17); cutting against it, that average is still falling, down 4.9% over 90 days, though the decline is gradually flattening from -5.1% yesterday. This is an early-recovery configuration, price reclaiming the trend line before the line turns up, which is why the score is only modestly positive. Valuation is neutral for the lean: the 200-week multiple of 1.27 is mid-range, price is 33% below its all-time high, the Puell Multiple of 1.28 puts miner revenue in a normal band, and the Pi-Cycle gap of -55% is far from the zone historically seen near cycle tops (context only, not scored). Macro is the clearest cross-current: the US 10-year yield is 5.29% against a fed funds rate of 3.63%, a meaningful competing return for risk assets, and The Block (29 September) cited rising yields and crude prices as headwinds for non-yielding assets. Structural holdings reinforce the lean, with cumulative spot ETF net inflows of about $57.7B, public companies holding roughly 1.28M BTC, and Santiment data reported by KuCoin on 30 September showing wallets holding 10–10,000 BTC adding about 41,000 BTC over ten days to roughly 67.9% of supply. The lean would strengthen if the 200-day slope turned positive, and would flip toward neutral or bearish if price fell back below that average while long yields stayed this high.

team_notes.marketing: Lean into non-stablecoin and active-trader channels: a +34% 90-day move, bitcoin's strongest quarter since late 2024 (per CoinDesk) and recent multi-billion spot ETF inflows give campaigns a credible, sourced recovery story. With Fear & Greed at 74 and funding turning positive again, sentiment is already warm, so lead with trend, institutional participation and product value rather than FOMO urgency, and avoid 'confirmed bull market' claims while breadth is 49% and conviction is medium (67/100). Keep stablecoin-first channels defended and some spend flexible ahead of the 27–28 October FOMC meeting.
